item.title: Wheelchair user completes historic bungee jump in Nepal
item.description: Deepa Devkota from Sindhuli District has become the first Nepali woman living with a disability to complete a wheelchair bungee jump at the Bhotekoshi River in Sindhupalchok District.

item.title: Sixteen days of activism amid the rise of digital harm across Africa
item.description: Across Africa, Reporters Without Borders has documented sustained online harassment and surveillance targeting women journalists in West Africa, noting that digital abuse has become an emerging barrier to press freedom.

item.title: As U.S.-Venezuela tensions rise, Trinidad & Tobago thumbs its nose at CARICOM
item.description: Criticism around the prime minister’s posturing, which academic Richard Drayton called “defiantly, even rudely, anti-Caricom,” started in September, when the U.S. began to assert its military presence in the region.

item.title: Mass shooting at Hanukkah celebration at Australia’s Bondi Beach shows the best and worst of humanity
item.description: Selfless acts at the scene were shared and praised by countless people online. One hero of the day tackled one of the gunmen and took his rifle from him.

item.title: Kenyan filmmaker Emily Nderitu shows the world how to talk about climate change in Africa
item.description: "We’re not short of knowledge or courage in Africa. We’re short of recognition. Storytelling can fix that. It can close the gap between visibility and value."

item.title: ‘The light plays tricks on us’: Trinidadian photographer Marlon Rouse’s ‘Sacred Objects, Fruit of the Land’
item.description: Rouse’s bold exploration rejects the familiar language of appetite, abundance and hospitality in favour of enquiry and even estrangement. The photos consider the fruit as organism rather than product.

item.title: The Tomorrow Club aims to support and mentor young writers amid polarity and tech-driven chaos
item.description: “The youth should never believe that history is written only by the victors, or that it can be permanently manipulated through narrative wars.”

item.title: Senegal: Where women’s bodies belong to everyone but themselves
item.description: In Senegal, women who are victims of rape can be condemned for trying to take control of their lives. Society decides what is best for women.

item.title: Learning feminism before knowing its name: Verse’s story from Myanmar
item.description: “Through film, I want people to feel empathy to see women’s emotions, existence, and oppression in new ways. My mind is always thinking for them.”

item.title: Japanese pop culture is sexually explicit, but sex education is wanting
item.description: Japan’s challenge is to reconcile the desire to preserve creative and erotic expression with the need to ensure that public spaces respect the differences among humankind.
